subject.title: fix(config): improve validation error messages with line numbers, bracket paths, and received values

question: What received-value disclosure contract should terminal config-validation diagnostics use when the validated effective value differs from the literal root-file value?
rationale: Raw values are safer but can be false after includes, environment substitution, or migration; effective values are accurate but can expand sensitive data, and repository policy does not define which tradeoff this new terminal surface should adopt.

options.title: Show only verified-safe exact values
options.body: Use the effective validation input only when it matches a safely classified literal and omit the received-value hint for substituted, included, migrated, SecretRef, or otherwise ambiguous values.

options.title: Drop received-value hints
options.body: Land bracket paths and line locations while omitting received values until a schema-aware sensitivity contract exists.

options.title: Allow effective values broadly
options.body: Print effective values after expanding the sensitive-path contract and adding explicit coverage for environment, include, plugin-schema, and SecretRef disclosures.

recommendation.title: Show only verified-safe exact values
recommendation.body: Use the effective validation input only when it matches a safely classified literal and omit the received-value hint for substituted, included, migrated, SecretRef, or otherwise ambiguous values.

likelyOwner.reason: BunsDev’s recent merged work owns the config-validation diagnostic surface being extended and is the strongest available routing candidate for its display contract.
